Subject: VPC streaming budget & fallback plan

Hi Alice / Somni infra team — great conversation earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have an actionable plan for the private deployment POC.

High-level requirements you confirmed on the call:
- Streaming inference (server-sent events) for low-latency transcript updates
- P95 end-to-end token latency target: ~80ms inside their primary region (us-west)
- Sustained concurrency target: 600 concurrent streaming sessions, burst to 1,000 for 2–5min
- Throughput: ~45K tokens/sec aggregate during peak; average expected ~12K tokens/sec
- VPN termination at customer edge (AWS TGW) with egress via AWS us-west-2

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Somni to provide VPN termination IP, peering point, and maintenance window for POC testing.
2) Team to run a short iperf3 and traceroute from the VPN endpoint to our private endpoint (we'll provide a test instance).
3) We need an initial sample of request/response sizes (avg tokens per request) to size KV cache and batching.

Proposed Redwood deliverables (POC baseline):
- Baseline SLO proposal and runbook (attached: slo_proposal.pdf)
- Network trace collection guidance and a lightweight trace collector (attachment: network_latency_trace.txt stub)
- Mutual action plan with milestones (attached: mutual_action_plan.xlsx)

Next steps
- Alice: share VPN details + point of contact (by Wed 6/2)
- Somni infra: run iperf/traceroute and share raw outputs into the Drive folder above
- Neha (SE): can you validate the targets below and propose a pressure-test plan?

Thanks — happy to hop back on a quick 30-min session to walk through the test plan.

—

2) If we see occasional p99 spikes >200ms, what fallback behavior do you recommend for streaming sessions?

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: RE: VPC streaming budget & fallback plan — SE validation + test plan

Ben / Marissa — summarized technical assessment and proposed test plan below. Long story short: feasible with the following constraints and measurement plan.

Quick assessment
- Tokenization/encoding overhead: ~4–7ms per request on server (depends on model variant and batching); negligible relative to network for small responses but matters at very low-latency targets.
- Expected added hop from Somni forwarding appliance: 5–10ms (account for in p95 budget).

Proposed SLOs (POC baseline)
- Client-observed P95 (end-to-end, including vpn+forwarding): <= 100ms
- Client-observed P99 (end-to-end): <= 200ms (with documented acceptable transient spikes up to 300ms for <0.1% requests)
- Sustained concurrent streaming sessions: validate at 600 sessions with 10 requests/sec average per session (conservative for their 50–200ms inter-event behavior)
- Burst capacity: validate to 1,000 concurrent sessions for 5 minutes with graceful degradation (queue + shed policy)

Test plan (high level)
1) Network baseline: Somni runs iperf3 (UDP & TCP) and traceroute to the test endpoint; collect RTT distributions and packet loss. (They'll upload traces to Drive.)
2) Latency injection: Run a controlled traffic generator from Somni endpoint that mimics their streaming pattern (600 sustained, ramp to 1,000 in 3 mins). Capture end-to-end timestamps from client and server.
3) KV cache / batching profile: provide a small sample corpus to benchmark batching benefit and tok/sec gains.
4) Streaming correctness: verify reconnect behavior and per-event ordering during transient spikes.

Runbook & fallback recommendations
- If p99 > 250ms for >0.5% of requests: enable fallback to smaller model variant or reduce response chunk size to cut tokenization time.
- If sustained packet loss >1%: propose switching to a regional Dedicated pool (reserve capacity) and enable degraded streaming mode that sends keepalive-only updates until recovery.

Attachments: brief SLO proposal (slo_proposal.pdf) and a sample collector config (network_latency_trace.txt).

I'll draft a short mutual action plan for the POC milestone and upload it to the shared Drive. Recommend a 2-week POC window with an initial test week and a stabilization week.

—
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
[Attachment: slo_proposal.pdf (application/pdf)]
